claims: Rick Pitino was born in 1952.
Rick Pitino is a Hall of Fame basketball coach.
Rick Pitino is the first coach to win NCAA championships at two different schools.
Rick Pitino won the 1996 NCAA championship with Kentucky.
Rick Pitino won the 2013 NCAA championship with Louisville.
Rick Pitino's 50-year career includes head coaching roles at BU, Providence, Kentucky, Louisville, Iona, and St. John's.
Rick Pitino had NBA stints at the Knicks and Celtics.
Rick Pitino was head coach at Boston University from 1978 to 1983.
Rick Pitino began his head coaching career at Boston University.
Rick Pitino was head coach at Providence College from 1985 to 1987.
Rick Pitino led the Friars to the 1987 Final Four.
Rick Pitino was head coach of the New York Knicks from 1987 to 1989.
Rick Pitino was head coach at University of Kentucky from 1989 to 1997.
Rick Pitino won the 1996 National Championship with University of Kentucky.
Rick Pitino reached three Final Fours with University of Kentucky.
Rick Pitino served as head coach and team president of the Boston Celtics from 1997 to 2001.
Rick Pitino was head coach at University of Louisville from 2001 to 2017.
Rick Pitino won the 2013 National Championship with University of Louisville (later vacated).
Rick Pitino reached three Final Fours with University of Louisville.
Rick Pitino coached Panathinaikos from 2018 to 2020.
Rick Pitino was head coach at Iona University from 2020 to 2023.
Rick Pitino led the Gaels to NCAA tournament appearances.
Rick Pitino has been head coach at St. John's University since 2023.
Rick Pitino is currently leading the Red Storm.
Rick Pitino has 6 Final Fours (1 Providence, 3 Kentucky, 2 Louisville).
Rick Pitino is the first coach to lead three different schools to the Final Four.
Rick Pitino has over 890 wins as of March 2026.
Rick Pitino's tenure at Louisville ended following a 2017 FBI investigation into college basketball corruption.
The 2017 FBI investigation led to the vacating of 123 wins at Louisville, including the 2012-2015 seasons.
